title: Refinement, estimation, and the ticket that was not ready to start

videos.script: On Monday, Ana picks up ticket 35. Its title is: pay online. There is no description. It looks simple. {{monday}} On Tuesday she has a payment form, and a question. Card, or Pix, or both? Nobody knows. {{tuesday}} On Wednesday she finds out the bakery has no account with any payment company yet, and that refunds are done by hand, at the bank. Everything she built assumed the opposite. {{wednesday}} Three days of work, and most of it goes in the bin. Not because Ana did anything wrong, but because the questions were asked in the wrong week. {{waste}} This lesson is about asking them earlier. {{earlier}} You will learn what makes a ticket ready to start, and what to do when you pick one up and find it is not. {{ready}} You will learn refinement, the regular conversation where a team turns a vague wish into tickets somebody can actually start, and how to split a big ticket into slices a customer can use. {{refine}} And you will learn estimation: story points, planning poker, and the thing most people miss about it, which is that the number matters much less than the conversation it starts. {{title}}
